headline: Constellation Energy Q2 beats + raises FY26 EPS guide to $11.50-$12.50 (from $11.00-$12.00); signs 920 MW of new long-term nuclear PPAs with investment-grade customers; +6.5% pre-market
summary: CEG reported Q2 2026 pre-open Aug 6: EPS beat consensus and management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $11.50-$12.50 (midpoint $12.00) from $11.00-$12.00 — new midpoint above Street $11.63. CFO Shane Smith cited 'expanded platform, operational execution and disciplined capital allocation.' The quarter added 920 MW of newly signed long-term nuclear PPAs with a diverse set of investment-grade customers, extending the datacenter-nuclear PPA book on top of the existing Microsoft/Meta agreements. Base EPS expected to compound >20% CAGR 2026-2029 on nuclear + natural gas + geothermal portfolio. Shares +6.56% to ~$282.50 pre-market. Read-through positive for VST, TLN, NEE, GEV (turbine follow-through), and CCJ/LEU (fuel cycle).

headline: Talen Energy Q2 2026: $374M adj EBITDA, $212M adj FCF; raises 2026 guide + lifts 2027-2028 outlooks after closing Cornerstone gas acquisition; AWS Susquehanna PPA book ~$18B thru 2042
summary: TLN reported Q2 2026 AMC Aug 5: Adjusted EBITDA $374M, adjusted free cash flow $212M. Company raised full-year 2026 guidance and increased 2027 and 2028 outlooks following the closing of the Cornerstone Acquisition (~2.6 GW of natural gas from Waterford / Darby / Lawrenceburg). Anchor commercial contract remains the expanded AWS PPA — up to 1,920 MW of Susquehanna nuclear power delivered to AWS datacenters through 2042 (~$18B revenue). Positions TLN as one of the cleanest pure-play reads on nuclear-scarcity-meets-datacenter-demand alongside CEG. Read-through: positive for VST (Meta 20-year PPA framework), NEE (Iowa/Duane Arnold restart optionality), and demand-side for GEV/ETN/VRT.

headline: Oklo's Groves Isotope Test Reactor in Texas reaches criticality — DOE confirms self-sustaining chain reaction; milestone for SMR / advanced-reactor commercialization ahead of Aurora COLA review
summary: Energy Department announced Thursday Aug 6 that Oklo's Groves Isotope Test Reactor in Texas has reached 'criticality' — the point at which a nuclear chain reaction becomes self-sustaining enough to produce a steady release of energy. First operational advanced-reactor milestone for OKLO ahead of the Aurora reactor's NRC Combined License Application review. Groves is the radioisotope pilot (agreement signed with DOE in May 2026) and is a separate physical asset from the commercial Aurora product, but the criticality event de-risks Oklo's execution narrative and materially advances the 'SMR commercial in the 2030s' timeline the market has priced. Read-through: positive for OKLO, SMR (NuScale peer read-through), CCJ/LEU (HALEU fuel demand). Watch for a re-rating in the SMR complex on the print.

headline: Sandisk fiscal Q4 blowout: revenue $8.97B +372% YoY / +51% QoQ, GAAP net income $6.90B ($43.97 EPS), gross margin 84.6%; Q1 FY27 guide $10.3-10.8B — 2/3 of sequential growth from pricing, not volume
summary: SanDisk (SNDK) reported Q4 fiscal 2026 AMC Aug 5: revenue $8.97B (+372% YoY, +51% QoQ) vs consensus, GAAP net income $6.90B / GAAP EPS $43.97, gross margin 84.6% (record). FY26 revenue $20.25B (+175% YoY); GAAP net income $11.43B vs $1.64B net loss prior year. Q1 FY27 guide: revenue $10.3-10.8B, non-GAAP EPS $44-46 — implies further sequential acceleration into the memory supercycle. Management said Q4 sequential growth was ~1/3 volume, ~2/3 pricing — NAND / enterprise SSD pricing tightening validates the MU / SK hynix / Samsung HBM+DRAM+NAND supply-constrained-through-2028 framing. Sandisk shares initially fell ~8% AH on high-multiple expectations, but the print is unambiguously bullish for the memory complex. Read-through: MU, 000660.KS, 005930.KS.

headline: Datadog -20% pre-market despite Q2 beat + raised FY guide: revenue $1.12B (vs $1.08B est), EPS $0.65 (vs $0.58), FY26 EPS $2.50-$2.54 (from $2.36-$2.44) — but Q3 revenue guide flags growth deceleration; largest single-day drop on record
summary: DDOG reported Q2 pre-open Aug 6: revenue $1.12B beat $1.08B est, EPS $0.65 beat $0.58 est, customers >$100k ARR grew to ~4,720 from 3,850 YoY. FY26 EPS raised to $2.50-$2.54 (from $2.36-$2.44). Despite the double beat and guide raise, shares fell as much as 20% pre-market — Q3 revenue guide $1.135-$1.145B implies growth deceleration from Q2's pace, and the print landed against Bernstein's pre-print Q3 caution note. Read-through: pockets of AI-tied SaaS multiple compression (recall NET reports today AMC, ~$665M est) — but not a datacenter-buildout tell; DDOG's story is expense discipline / competitive pressure from CRWD's Falcon LogScale + observability-native AI features, not infrastructure demand. Neutral read for AI-infrastructure names.

headline: SoftBank Group Q1 FY27: revenue ¥1.815T (+9% YoY, Q1 record); AI segment guided +30% CAGR through FY27; ARM subsidiary — AGI CPU orders >$2B (vs original ~$1B combined FY26+FY27 guide)
summary: SoftBank Group reported Q1 FY27 Aug 6: revenue ¥1.814.7T (+9% YoY, Q1 record), operating income ¥302.3B, net income ¥150.1B. SoftBank Corp AI segment guided +30% CAGR through FY27. Read-through comes from Arm Holdings: AGI CPU (Arm's server CPU line) cumulative customer demand now >$2B (up from ~$1B original combined FY26+FY27 revenue guide); first-generation AGI CPU gross margins high-30s to low-40s% in FY27-28, path to 50% over time. Arm shipments to several customers already underway; capacity locked in for >$1B of early deployments. Read-through: bullish for ARM data-center CPU thesis (competitive share vs INTC Xeon / AMD EPYC in hyperscaler / neocloud silicon selection); NVDA GB-series continues to co-package Arm cores.

headline: Palantir analyst tape stays hot post-blowout: Cantor lifts PT to $156 (from $138, Neutral), following DA Davidson $200 / Citi $245 / Wedbush $230 / UBS $220 — consensus Buy rating held by 20 analysts
summary: Post Palantir Q2 print (rev $1.94B +93% YoY, US commercial +149%, FY guide raised to $8.15-8.16B), the analyst tape kept adding upgrades into Thursday. Cantor Fitzgerald's Thomas Blakey raised PT to $156 from $138 while maintaining Neutral. Follows DA Davidson to $200 (from $175, Buy), Citi to $245 (from $200, Buy), Wedbush $230, UBS to $220 (from $200), Deutsche upgrade to Buy $200. Per Public.com, 20 analysts hold a Buy consensus rating as of Aug 6. Stock consolidating post the +29.5% Tuesday pop; retracement modest. Watch for sector rotation into other 'sovereign AI + defense' names (BKSY, GOVX, VRT) on any pause.

headline: Pre-open macro calendar Aug 6: Challenger July job cuts, initial jobless claims (prev 197k, cons ~203k), Q2 preliminary nonfarm productivity (+0.7% cons vs +0.3% prior); SpaceX IPO lockup expires today
summary: Thursday Aug 6 economic calendar includes: Challenger job cuts July (prior YoY -4.5%), initial jobless claims for week ended Aug 1 (prev 197k / 57-year low bounced +9k; cons ~203k), continuing claims, and Q2 preliminary nonfarm productivity (cons +0.7% vs prior +0.3%). Fed left rates unchanged at 3.50-3.75% July 29; next meeting September. SpaceX IPO lockup expires today Aug 6 — watch for share supply. Overnight macro: quiet after Wednesday's Middle East tanker headlines faded; S&P futures +0.11%, Nasdaq-100 -0.58%, Dow +0.22%, Russell flat pre-open — a modest tech tone-down as DDOG's 20% drop pressures observability / SaaS names.
